triggers: a Metal engine risks the 'unsynchronized mlx fp16 array reads return garbage; zero-copy from foreign pointers segfaults' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on Apple M-series Metal: unsynchronized mlx fp16 array reads return garbage; zero-copy from foreign pointers segfaults

problem.target: Apple Silicon (M-series), mlx 0.32 C++ API / Metal 4 toolchains
problem.statement: unsynchronized mlx fp16 array reads return garbage; zero-copy from foreign pointers segfaults

payload.attempted: Reading quantized_matmul output via array.data<uint16_t>() after eval(), and constructing mlx arrays from engine-owned MTLBuffer pointers via the void* zero-copy constructor.
payload.lesson: Always bridge buffers through copying constructors plus an astype(float32)+eval for the last-mile read-back, or allocate through mlx::core::allocator::malloc when zero-copy is truly needed.

established_fact.mechanism: On the Metal backend, array buffers are not host-synchronized by eval for direct fp16 data reads (an astype(float32)+eval round-trip is), and the zero-copy constructor only tolerates pointers obtained from mlx's own allocator - foreign MTLBuffer/malloc pointers are treated as GPU addresses.

payload.observed: data<uint16_t>() returned wrong values (0.0/-4.5 where -1040/-32 expected) even after eval; the zero-copy constructor segfaulted in memcpy on malloc-backed pointers.
payload.root_cause: On the Metal backend, array buffers are not host-synchronized by eval for direct fp16 data reads (an astype(float32)+eval round-trip is), and the zero-copy constructor only tolerates pointers obtained from mlx's own allocator - foreign MTLBuffer/malloc pointers are treated as GPU addresses.
